# Nextra AI-ready fixture

This is a real Nextra 4 documentation site, not a static screenshot or a configuration snippet.

The browser experience remains owned by Nextra. `next-ai-ready` reads the same MDX files and adds
discovery and retrieval endpoints for AI systems.

## What this fixture proves

- Nextra still renders the human-facing documentation UI.
- `/llms.txt` lists the documentation pages.
- `/getting-started.md` returns clean Markdown.
- `Accept: text/markdown` negotiates the same page as Markdown.
- Unknown browser routes remain real `404` responses.

Continue with [Getting started](/getting-started).

<!-- END / -->

<!-- BEGIN /getting-started -->
# Getting started
URL: https://nextra-fixture.example/getting-started
Updated: 2026-09-28

# Getting started

Install the public package beside an existing Nextra 4 application:

```bash
pnpm add next-ai-ready zod@^4
pnpm exec next-ai-ready init
```

Keep Nextra's plugin in place, then wrap its resulting Next.js config:

```js
import nextra from "nextra"
import { withAiReady } from "next-ai-ready/config"

const withNextra = nextra({})
const nextConfig = withNextra({})

export default withAiReady({ agentReadable: true })(nextConfig)
```

Build both representations from the same MDX source:

```bash
pnpm exec next-ai-ready build
pnpm build
```

The HTML page remains available at `/getting-started`; its explicit Markdown representation is
available at `/getting-started.md`.

## FAQ

### Does next-ai-ready replace Nextra?

No. Nextra keeps rendering the documentation interface while next-ai-ready adds machine-readable resources.

### Does this fixture enable callable agent actions?

No. It intentionally validates only the knowledge plane so the first integration stays small and reviewable.
